c.tagline: A tri-border Amazon gateway where Colombia, Brazil, and Peru meet along the world's largest river

card: Accepted at larger hotels; cash is essential for markets, boats, and small eateries

taxi.fareNote: Moto-taxis are the fastest way around the small town center

emergency.note: 123 connects to police, fire, and medical services across Colombia

religion: indigenous spiritual traditions (practiced alongside Christianity in some communities)
walk: Central Leticia is small and walkable; reaching the rainforest reserves, Monkey Island, or Tabatinga (Brazil) requires a boat, taxi, or short walk across the unmarked border

safety.safety: Generally safe in the town center; exercise standard caution near the borders and when traveling by boat after dark
safety.crime: Petty theft can occur in markets; most visitors experience no issues traveling with a reputable tour operator

hood_landmark.Town Center / Santander Park: Santander Park and the Cathedral of Leticia
hood_landmark.Tabatinga Border (Brazil): The open land border crossing into Tabatinga, Brazil
hood_landmark.Km 11 (Reserva Natural Tanimboca area): The Tanimboca canopy and rainforest reserve outside town

avoid.reason: Avoid the unlit riverfront port area and the border backstreets toward Tabatinga late at night, where smuggling-related crime occurs.
Book jungle excursions only with registered guides and steer clear of remote river stretches at night due to trafficking activity.

hood_desc: The compact commercial core around Santander Park, with the cathedral, most hotels, and restaurants; the natural base for exploring the region.
The Amazon River waterfront, where cargo boats, tour operators, and river-market vendors set the rhythm of daily life.
The seamless, unmarked border crossing into Brazil, a short walk or moto-taxi ride away, worth a stroll for the tri-border novelty.
A rainforest reserve just outside town offering canopy walkways and overnight jungle lodges without a long river journey.
A national park reached by river boat, protecting primary Amazon rainforest and offering multi-day guided treks.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only.

transit.sys: Moto-taxis and small local buses within town; river boats connect to outlying reserves and villages
transit.hours: Roughly 6am-9pm for local transit; river boat schedules vary
transit.map: Not centrally published; hotels and tour agencies arrange river transport
transit.note: There are no roads connecting Leticia to the rest of Colombia; all overland routes are by river or air

transport.air: Alfredo Vásquez Cobo International Airport (LET), about 10 min from town, with flights from Bogotá
transport.bus: No long-distance road connections to the rest of Colombia (surrounded by rainforest and rivers)
transport.ferry: Riverboats connect Leticia to Iquitos, Peru and other Amazon river towns (multi-day journey)
transport.car: Not applicable for reaching Leticia; local roads within town are limited

net.m: Moderate 3G/4G in town, minimal coverage on the river or in the rainforest
net.fwn: Wifi available in hotels, though speeds are modest
net.ap: A Claro or Movistar tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is appreciated for jungle guides and boat operators
tip.r: 10% if not already included in the bill
